mathgap.title: Sequential Transfer Application
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X gives N items to Y", immediately subtract N from X's current count and add N to Y's count, using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any direct transfer statement without conditions (e.g., "X gives N ... to Y").
mathgap.example: Subtracting N from the giver but forgetting to add N to the receiver, resulting in a net loss of items.

mathgap.title: Signed Interpretation of "has K more than"
mathgap.principle: Interpret "A has K more than B" as the signed equation A − B = K (or A = B + K), preserving the order of names.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a comparative statement of the form "A has K more than B" appears.
mathgap.example: Reversing the direction and writing B − A = K instead of A − B = K.

mathgap.title: Signed Equality for Difference Statements
mathgap.principle: For statements of the form "The number of items that A has more than B is equal to the difference between the number of items that C and D have", interpret as (A − B) = (C − D), preserving the order on each side.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a statement equates a "has more than" difference to a "difference between" expression.
mathgap.example: Treating the right-hand side as |C − D| (absolute difference) and losing the sign.

mathgap.title: Current‑Count Constraint for "has N"
mathgap.principle: A statement "A has N items" fixes A's count at that point in the narrative, after any earlier transfers or updates; later statements may modify A's count, but this statement defines the current value.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a direct count statement appears.
mathgap.example: Assuming the count is an initial value and ignoring earlier transfers that already changed the person's count.

mathgap.title: Iterative Substitution and Propagation
mathgap.principle: Whenever a variable's value becomes known, substitute it into all pending equations and simplify, propagating the information throughout the system until all values are resolved.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After solving any equation that determines a person's count, update all other equations that involve that person.
mathgap.example: Solving an equation but not substituting the known value into other equations, leaving variables unresolved.

mathgap.title: Consistency Check After Solving
mathgap.principle: After assigning values to all variables, verify each original statement—including transfers, direct counts, comparative equations, and conditional transfers—to ensure no contradictions remain.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After the solution is derived, before presenting the final answer.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution without verifying that all conditional transfers satisfy their conditions.

mathgap.title: Chronological Evaluation of Comparative Statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret comparative statements using the counts as they exist at that point in the narrative, after any earlier transfers or updates, not using initial counts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any comparative statement that appears after earlier statements have potentially changed counts.
mathgap.example: Using a person's initial count for a comparison that appears later in the narrative, ignoring prior transfers.

mathgap.title: Query‑Focused Subsystem Extraction
mathgap.principle: Identify the subset of equations and statements that involve the queried person directly or through a chain of dependencies, and solve only that subsystem, ignoring unrelated statements.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When the problem contains many extraneous statements not needed for the queried individual's final count.
mathgap.example: Attempting to solve the entire system of equations, including many unrelated variables, leading to unnecessary complexity and potential errors.

mathgap.title: Conditional Transfer Evaluation
mathgap.principle: For statements of the form "If X has more than N items, X will transfer their items to Y", evaluate the condition using X's current count at that point; if true, move all of X's items to Y (set X's count to 0 and add the transferred amount to Y). Apply this in chronological order.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a conditional transfer clause appears ("If ... has more than ... then X transfers all to Y").
mathgap.example: Always performing the transfer regardless of the condition, or transferring only N items instead of all of X's items.

mathgap.title: Equal Redistribution Handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says "X and Y redistribute their items to ensure each has an equal amount", pool their current counts and assign each half of the total (total/2) as the new count for both X and Y. For statements like "X splits all her items equally among A and B", set X's count to 0 and give each of A and B half of X's previous count. Assume totals are even unless the puzzle explicitly allows fractions.
mathgap.when_to_apply: For any redistribution or equal‑split statements involving two parties, including "redistribute" and "splits all ... equally among" constructions.
mathgap.example: Interpreting redistribution as a one‑way transfer (moving all items from X to Y) instead of splitting the total equally.

mathgap.description: Swapped direction in "has K more than" statements
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model often treats the phrase as symmetric and writes B − A = K instead of A − B = K.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of names as given: interpret "A has K more than B" as A − B = K.

mathgap.why_it_happens: The model defaults to the common "absolute difference" interpretation, losing sign information.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Preserve the signed order when interpreting "difference between X and Y" as X − Y.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the chronological order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes all counts are static and applies transfers out of order.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process statements sequentially; each transfer uses the counts as they exist at that point.

mathgap.description: Treating "has N" as an initial count regardless of position
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model assumes such statements set a starting value and ignores earlier updates.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply "has N" as a constraint on the current count after any prior statements have been processed.

mathgap.description: Assuming all "more than" differences must be positive
mathgap.why_it_happens: The model expects "more than" to indicate a positive gap and rejects negative values.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Allow the signed difference to be negative if earlier constraints force it; do not force positivity.
